units.text: INT. MOVING VAN - DAY
CLOSE ON the back of a rattling box truck, packed to the roof with old furniture wrapped in grey blankets.
We see a walnut dresser from the 1920s, a mirror in a gilded frame, and a tall grandfather clock lashed with orange straps.
Rain hammers on the metal roof.
The road outside is wet and grey.
It is a very dull morning.
SAM, 30s, sits on a crate near the back door, looking worried.
He checks the straps again.
Next to him JEN, 20s, is writing on a clipboard.
In the front, through a little window, we see BIG DAVE driving and MO in the passenger seat eating chips.
Jen, are you sure the clock is secure? It's worth like ten thousand dollars.
units.name: SAM

units.text: He has checked it three times, Sam. He is very sure.
units.name: JEN

units.text: I'm just saying, if it falls, we all lose our jobs.
units.name: SAM

units.text: The van hits a pothole.
The clock RATTLES.
The mirror TINKLES.
She grabs the clipboard.
He grabs the clock.
Sorry about that, folks!
units.name: BIG DAVE

units.text: Dave, watch the road!
units.name: MO

units.text: Lightning FLASHES through the cracks in the door and, for a second, we see everyone's faces lit up in white.
In the back, behind the dresser, a hand moves.
It is an old woman's hand, wrinkled and thin, and she pushes a blanket aside.
This is MRS. K, 80s, the owner of all this furniture, who has been hiding in the van the whole time.
Mrs. K?
units.name: SAM

units.text: I wasn't going to let you take Henry's clock without me.
units.name: MRS. K

units.text: Ma'am, you can't be back here. It's not safe.
units.name: JEN

units.text: I have been safe for eighty years. I would like to be something else.
units.name: MRS. K

units.text: The phone in Jen's pocket BUZZES.
She looks at it, he looks at her, and she answers.
Hello? Yes, we have her. No, she's fine.
units.name: JEN

units.text: Jen, it's Lou at dispatch. The client's daughter just called. Her mother is missing. Please tell me she's in the van.
units.name: LOU

units.text: She is in the van.
units.name: JEN

units.text: Oh thank God.
units.name: LOU

units.text: The van HONKS and SCREECHES to a halt.
Everyone slides forward.
The clock tips.
Sam catches it, barely.
They all breathe.
A pause.
The rain softens.
Out the back window a rainbow, small and surprised, appears over a wet parking lot.
Henry always loved a rainbow.
units.name: MRS. K

units.text: Sam looks at her.
She looks at him.
They both understand something they cannot say.
We're here! Everybody out!
units.name: BIG DAVE

units.text: The back door RATTLES OPEN.
Light pours in.
